doc: The figure's cases (quota-model 67 §11): standings in short form, the classes and bare lanes' settings the routes come from, the sizing view (_sizing_fleet_view's shape: whole-window dollars) and the fleet expected, compared as a subset. Made-up names and numbers. Times are seconds from `now`: a window's resets_in, an account's age.

cases.name: 67 §5 worked example
notes: Provider P is anthropic (R = Opus, the reference; F = Fable weighed at 2.3; S = Sonnet 5 unweighed), Q is gpt (T its reference). A, B, C, G, K are sub-A, sub-B, sub-C, gpt-G, gpt-K.

Two corrections to 67 §5's arithmetic, both from rules 67 §6 states itself. (1) A stop_at is per route, so the frontier member's stop_at 7d 80 caps A (and C) as well as B: A's main window is cap 80, capacity 80 x 13.0435 = $1,043.48, room 30 x 13.0435 = $391.30, and A takes room $391.30, not $455. (2) A stop_at naming 7d names the unscoped seven_day window (_stop_window), not scoped:Fable, so B's scoped window keeps cap 100: capacity and room 100 x 1.3 = $130, not $104.
lane:default has no model of its own lane weighed, so it is valued at each window's mix, as fast is (67 §11).

cases.name: one account, one window: left_pct is (cap - used) / cap whatever the model
notes: Valued at Opus ($10/pt), at Fable ($4/pt) or at the mix ($8/pt), 35 of 100 used leaves 65 %.
The bare opus lane has two weighed models of its own: it is valued at the one with more dollars, Opus 5.5 ($10/pt), not Opus 4.1 ($6/pt).

cases.name: cap from a route's stop_at: by period, by scope, effective, at or above 100, and 0
notes: Fable is $5/pt on seven_day (used 20) and $2/pt on scoped:Fable (used 10).
by-period (7d 50): seven_day 250/150, scoped 200/180 -> 200/150.
by-scope (Fable 40): seven_day 500/400, scoped 80/60 -> 80/60.
effective (60): seven_day 300/200, scoped 120/100 -> 120/100.
over (7d 150): cap 100 -> 200/180. zero (7d 0): seven_day 0/0 -> 0/0, no left_pct; negative (7d -10) is cap 0 as well. A stop_at reached on a counted window is room 0 by the arithmetic, not refused.
The accounts level takes the highest cap any route allows: the bare lanes allow 100.

cases.name: the whole proxy takes the highest cap any route allows
notes: Every route names seven_day: a 7d 50, b effective 60, every bare lane 7d 70. The proxy level caps the account at 70: at the mix ($8/pt), 560 / 400, 71.4 %.

cases.name: a held main window, a closed short window, both closed, a stale reading, a passed reset, a closed short scoped window
notes: Each account is $10/pt at Opus. held: seven_day at 100 (a hold reads 100): room 0, capacity kept, refused until its reset. resting: five_hour closed, seven_day at 40: room 600 counted, resting until the five_hour reset. both: room 0, refused until the later reset, not resting. stale: read 4000 s ago, counted at 40 and marked. reopened: seven_day read 100 but its reset has passed: it counts as reopened, used 0, as the dial check reads it (50 §1.4).

short-scoped: a 5-hour window scoped to Opus is closed; shorter than the main, it is a speed limit, not the scoped window of the min rule: lane:opus rests the account, room 600 counted. The whole proxy (unscoped) does not see it.

fable-spent: its weekly scoped:Fable window is spent, the main open: the scoped window is as long as the main, so lane:fable refuses the account (room 0 until that reset); lane:opus, which it does not bind, counts 600.
two-short: five_hour and a one-day window both closed: resting until the later reset.
gate-short: the provider's own gate is shut beside a closed five_hour: refused, not resting. own-gate: seven_day at 30 but shut by its own gate: it counts 100, refused.
lane:opus: capacity 10 x 1000, room 600 x 5 (resting, stale, short-scoped, fable-spent, two-short) + 1000 (reopened) = 4000, 40 %.

cases.name: a class whose two members reach one account values it at the higher-priority member
notes: fable-first runs Fable first: Fable's $5/pt on seven_day (40 used) and the scoped:Fable window ($2/pt, 50 used): min(500, 200) / min(300, 100) = 200 / 100. Opus first: $10/pt on seven_day alone, Opus having no scoped window: 1000 / 600.

cases.name: unmeasured, api, no main window, not sized, not read; a closed gate; a cycle pool as main
notes: Listed with why and never added: sub-U (no reading), runway (an api account), sub-N (a scoped window only), sub-S (seven_day few_steps; its own left_pct, 75 %, still shows on the accounts level, 67 §13 Q7).
gpt-X: codex's own gate is shut with seven_day at 30: refused, capacity kept ($20/pt: 2000), room 0, until the window's reset.
kimi: its monthly pool (1mo) is longer than its weekly window, so it is the main window: $1/pt, 30 used: 100 / 70.

kimi-2: its pool reads 100: room 0 by the arithmetic, but not refused, since the dial check reads only windows and never gates on the pool (K2). Its pool was read 4000 s ago, its windows now: stale by its main window.
kimi-3: its pool reads 100 and its five_hour is closed: the main window is not open, so it is refused, not resting, until the five_hour reset.
sub-R: its scoped:Fable window has no reading: listed for c, whose first member is the Fable lane, rather than counted on its main window alone.

cases.name: a no-window limit zeroes the bound selections only: a model limit by model and by lane scope, a pool for all; ended at until and at re-check
notes: sub-A: model:claude-sonnet-5-1 is not the member's model (claude-sonnet-5) but its lane scope is Sonnet: it refuses fast and lane:sonnet there, not o, lane:opus, lane:default or the proxy.
sub-A: model:claude-mystery-1 is in no scoped lane: it binds by its id alone, so nothing here (lane:default is at the mix, with no scope).
gpt-A: model:gpt-6.1-sol (not_entitled) refuses fast's gpt member, which runs it, and not o's, which runs gpt-6-astra.
kimi-A: pool:total_quota refuses every selection reaching it and the whole proxy; the accounts entry shows it refused.
sub-B: one limit past its until and one older than the owner's re-check: neither binds nor is listed.
Capacity is kept wherever room is zeroed.

cases.name: the default lane keeps §7's valuation; a model limit never binds it, a pool does
notes: claude-mystery-1 matches no scoped lane and is the most-dollared weighed model: the default lane is valued at it ($4/pt), as push 2 built (67 §7).
A limit on claude-mystery-1 leaves the default lane unrefused: one model's limit stops one of the many models that lane serves.
sub-P: a pool limit still refuses the default lane.

cases.name: a class whose higher-priority member a model limit binds is valued at the next member, and refused only when every member is bound
notes: Class s2: lane:sonnet (1) then lane:opus (2), both on sub-M and sub-N. A Sonnet limit on sub-M leaves the Opus member: valued at Opus, not refused.
On sub-N limits bind both members: refused, valued at the higher-priority member (Sonnet), until the first member frees: the Opus limit ends at +900, before the Sonnet one at +1800, so it is named.

cases.name: a window's refusal and a limit's: the later shows, an unknown end the latest; a limit refuses a resting account; the limit that ends last shows
notes: sub-W: seven_day spent, resetting in 600 s, and a Sonnet limit to 1800 s: the limit ends later, so it shows (until +1800).
sub-V: the mirror: seven_day spent, resetting in 300000 s, and the same limit: the window shows, no limit named.
sub-U: seven_day spent with no known reset and the same limit: an unknown end counts as later, the window shows.
sub-R: five_hour closed, seven_day open (resting) and a Sonnet limit: refused by the limit, not resting.
sub-T: two Sonnet-lane limits, ending in 1800 s and 3600 s: the later shows.

cases.name: a class member on the default lane is bound by its model's id, as the proxy refuses it
notes: Class d1: the default lane running claude-mystery-1 (1), then lane:sonnet (2). Only the bare default lane is exempt from a model limit (67 §9).
sub-E: a claude-mystery-1 limit binds the default-lane member: the account falls through to the Sonnet member.
sub-F: limits on claude-mystery-1 and claude-sonnet-5 bind both: refused, valued at the default-lane member, until the first member frees (+900).

cases.name: a class falls through by model id where no lane scope matches
notes: Class g2: two members on the gpt provider, gpt-6.1-sol (1) then gpt-6-astra (2); neither model is in a scoped lane.
gpt-B: a gpt-6.1-sol limit binds the first member by its id alone: the account is valued at gpt-6-astra, not refused.
